reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent static review against live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP (retail PE view_1), radare2 6.2.0 CFG and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast on retail igi.exe; candidate source read from this worktree. No game process was executed and no runtime behavior is claimed.
review_basis: Retail 0x004A9D28 was re-disassembled, re-decompiled and re-CFG'd through the live Binary Ninja view, independently recovered with radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast. The candidate is scripts/GameNatives/camera/004A9D28-Camera_ApplyBandFilter_18.cpp at sha256 1cfdc089918d31b8b0d3ba8c7740cc37465052830803c0146ecfa8c4ec571b79 (recorded implementation.signature: int32_t(int32_t arg1 @ 0x8) __pure Camera_ApplyBandFilter_18(void);). The evidence artifact digests are bound in this review.

checks.detail: BN models the single argument at [E+8] (`int32_t(int32_t arg1 @ 0x8)`); radare2 also reports arg_8h. The candidate's cdecl `context` is the [E+4] slot, so the read would come from the wrong stack word.

signature_comparison.rationale: Binary Ninja reports "int32_t(int32_t arg1 @ 0x8) __pure" at 0x004A9D28; radare2 recovers "fcn.004a9d28 (int32_t arg_8h);". Both tools place the entry at 0x004A9D28 and agree on the stack/register word count and cleanup; the difference is the level of type/argument-name detail, not the call frame. Candidate declaration: int32_t(int32_t arg1 @ 0x8) __pure Camera_ApplyBandFilter_18(void);. The candidate declaration is separately recorded as divergent below and does not satisfy the retail ABI.
